C-VIEWER-WINDOW-DRAG.Name: Restore host-window dragging from the fullscreen block viewer header
C-VIEWER-WINDOW-DRAG.ApprovalBasis: Owner report on 2026-11-10 that the table viewer makes the window impossible to move, plus standing delegated stabilization decisions. Diagnostic real-pointer evidence separates working canvas panning from a header that dispatches no native drag command.
C-VIEWER-WINDOW-DRAG.Summary: The body-level fullscreen viewer covers the ordinary title bar. Expose its header and title to the existing host drag-region mechanism and exclude its controls.

Goals.Goal: The viewer header and title initiate host-window dragging through the existing titlebar contract. Buttons, pan/zoom canvas, native resize edges and non-primary mouse buttons keep their existing actions.

Constraints.Item: Keep the current fullscreen overlay, content cloning, pan/zoom, controls, focus lifecycle, exports, app version and native permission set. No new native window or drag implementation, schema, dependency, retry, timeout, skip or coverage reduction. Do not change open user documents.

NonGoals.Item: No viewer redesign, native window conversion, drag/pan redesign or release.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red/green real-pointer browser evidence proves native drag command dispatch from header/title and no dispatch from controls, canvas, resize edge or a non-primary press. Existing viewer lifecycle, pan, zoom and focus tests remain green.

AffectedAreas.Area: M-012 BlockViewer, V-M-012; reuse the unchanged M-011 titlebar drag-region contract.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Viewer and macOS titlebar units, renderer build, Chromium/WebKit table/viewer gate and a fresh attributable QA build. Actual native window movement is a separate manual acceptance scenario.
